title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-26

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1969 show highlighted by a smoking Eleven → Lovelight and an inspired Clementine
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently praised for its manic energy, with the Eleven/Lovelight sequence, a fierce Death Don't Have No Mercy, and a standout Clementine jam earning top marks. The soundboard source is described as clean and well‑balanced, though a few reviewers note occasional mix fluctuations and limited high‑end “crunch”. Overall the show shines despite minor recording quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (30+) give 4–5 stars and celebrate the musical intensity, while recording comments are mostly positive with only occasional mix complaints, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean and balanced overall; missing some high‑end crunch, early‑show mix fluctuations, and occasional treble‑muddy sections, but generally solid for the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers note a seamless flow, especially the natural transition from Clementine into Dark Half/Help‑like jam and the tight Eleven → Lovelight pairing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for ripping his Gibson, delivering intense lead work (e.g., Dark Star pace, powerful soloing).
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as a beast; highlighted for bass lines like the So What quote in Clementine and overall “phil is a beast” performance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for joining Phil on a Spoonful jam during Lovelight (“Phil and Bobby hitting Spoonful”).
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard balance noted positively (Pigpen organ and keyboards well‑recorded), though no specific player named.
